8207cf72155de453d9aa611901bd308f.detailed_summary:
• Renewable and sustainable energy sources are two broad categories of energy sources used to meet the world's energy demands .
• Conventional and non-conventional energy sources differ in terms of availability, environmental impact, and technological maturity .
• Non-renewable energy sources can be used in green buildings to provide clean and reliable power, with water and heat as byproducts .
• Solar architecture is an architectural approach that takes in account the Sun to harness clean and renewable solar power .
• Passive solar heating is a design approach that utilizes the natural heat from the sun to provide indoor heating without the need for mechanical or electrical systems .
• The effectiveness of passive solar heating depends on the building's location, orientation, and the local climate .
• Passive solar collection involves using the building's design, orientation, and materials to optimize solar heat gain during the winter months .
• South-facing glass allows solar energy into the living space, where it directly and indirectly strikes thermal mass materials like masonry walls and floors .
• These materials help regulate temperature by absorbing excess heat during the day and releasing it slowly at night .
• Wind turbines are designed to start generating electricity at a certain minimum wind speed .
• They shut down at a higher wind speed (cut-out speed) to prevent damage .
• Even a small increase in wind speed can lead to a significant increase in power generation .
